items.title: The Roundup: Punishment
items.reason: A 109-minute South Korean police action-comedy about an illegal online gambling syndicate, with an investigation spanning Seoul and the Philippines. Screen Daily describes a brisk but formulaic mixture of police procedure, humor and fights, while RogerEbert.com details a pursuit and the final confrontation and criticizes underpowered action and generic characterization. AsianMovieWeb describes a notable knife fight involving the villain and recurring heavy-handed boxing-style clashes, but also investigative and comic passages. Consequently the whole-film action density is moderate-to-high rather than continuous; intense individual melee scenes do not substitute for density. The cybercrime investigation and international locations add some variety, while repetition of the series formula, thin supporting roles and a less distinctive finale are limitations. The villain's former military background does not make this a military-operation film, and unsanctioned boxing-style punches are not sports fighting. Descriptive DNA only; no final eligibility or score is inferred.
